newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen A shares end sharply lower, hit by bank.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen A shares end sharply lower, hit by bank.

text.p: Shenzhen's domestic currency A share market closed down sharply on Wednesday, the first session after the Hong Kong handover, driven down by heavy losses in market giant Shenzhen Development Bank, brokers said.
The index slid 18.30 points or 4.07 percent to 431.12 on turnover of 7.8 billion yuan compared with last Friday's 11.5 billion yuan. The index touched a low of 409.97.
Trading in the city's hard currency B shares will resume on Thursday due to the Hong Kong market holiday to mark the reversion of the former British colony to China at midnight on June 30.
"Sentiment was severely hurt by institutional dumping of Shenzhen Development Bank," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
"Falls in the bank pushed down the market and sparked heavy selling in a range of other shares," an analyst with Hainan Provincial Trust and Investment Co said in Shenzhen.

The company, China's only bank with a domestic listing, tumbled 1.61 yuan to 36.13 yuan after hitting an intra-session low of 34.00 yuan. Volume was 19 million shares, making it the most actively traded stock.

Brokers said the bank's fall was caused in part by a front-page report in the China Securities newspaper on Wednesday urging Shenzhen to re-compile its sub-index, in which the bank has a 33 percent weighting.
The sub-index, which was launched in early 1995, has never been revised and only covers 40 listed firms, the Beijing-based newspaper said.
The sub-index is no longer representative of the trend of the overall market after the steep rise in the number of companies on the southern China bourse over the past year, the paper said.
The number of companies represented in the sub-index should be expanded and the bank's weighting should be lowered, it said.
The sub-index fell 206.18 points or 4.06 percent to 4,875.27 by Wednesday's close.
Brokers said some institutional investors have been seeking to influence the market trend by manipulating prices of the bank's shares.
They also said Wednesday's plunge fostered speculation among investors that Beijing would soon introduce further policies to counter speculation.
"Negative rumours are swirling around the market," a trader said.
Most of the brokers said the Hong Kong handover was not a significant factor in the day's retreat.
"The (Hong Kong) handover is now no longer a factor in the Shenzhen market because investors have already been preparing for the event for a long time," the Guotai analyst said.
"But some investors interpret the passing of the handover as the end of a significant good news element for the market," an analyst at Xiangcai Securities Co said.
Brokers said they expected consolidation amid increasing volatility in the coming sessions.
Property developer Hong Kai Group was the biggest loser, plunging 1.57 yuan to its 10-percent limit-down at 14.12 yuan.
